subproblem.title: Hausdorff and mass measures under the blow-up map
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel measurable, a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0. Let Hⁿ = μHE[n], η := blowUpMap a λ, η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − a), and let dilation a λ be the contract's map y ↦ −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y (dilationCLM). Write ofReal(λ^{−n}) for ENNReal.ofReal(λ⁻¹ ^ n), _# for Measure.map and ⌞ for Measure.restrict. Then (i) η(M) is a Borel set; (ii) Hⁿ⌞η(M) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·(dilation a λ)_#(Hⁿ⌞M); (iii) ofReal(λ^{−n})·(dilation a λ)_#((Hⁿ⌞M) with density x ↦ ofReal θ(x)) = (Hⁿ⌞η(M)) with density y ↦ ofReal θ(a + λy).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (θ : Euclid P → ℝ) (a : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), MeasurableSet M → Measurable θ → 0 < lam → MeasurableSet (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap a lam '' M) ∧ μHE[n].restrict (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap a lam '' M) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • Measure.map (dilation a lam) (μHE[n].restrict M) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • Measure.map (dilation a lam) ((μHE[n].restrict M).withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (θ x))) = (μHE[n].restrict (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap a lam '' M)).withDensity (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (θ (a + lam • y)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (change of variables under the blow-up; the scaling of Hⁿ, (dc)(6) there, is re-derived here from Mathlib).
Notation: η := blowUpMap a λ, D := dilation a λ, Hⁿ := μHE[n], c := ofReal(λ^{−n}) = ENNReal.ofReal(λ⁻¹ ^ n).
1. (The map.) η = D as functions: λ⁻¹(y − a) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y (unfold blowUpMap, dilation, dilationCLM; smul_sub; abel). D is the composition of the homeomorphism y ↦ λ⁻¹y (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero, λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) with the translation z ↦ −λ⁻¹a + z (Homeomorph.addLeft); hence D is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P, in particular a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding). Moreover a + λ·D(x) = x for every x (smul_add, smul_neg, smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀, one_smul, abel).
2. (Part (i).) η(M) = D(M) is the image of a Borel set under a measurable embedding, hence Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image).
3. (Scaling of Hⁿ.) For every A ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(D(A)) = c·Hⁿ(A). Indeed D(A) = τ(m(A)) with m(y) := λ⁻¹y and τ(z) := −λ⁻¹a + z (Set.image_image). τ is an isometry (isometry_add_left), so Hⁿ(τ(B)) = Hⁿ(B) for all B (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). By Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ (λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) and Set.image_smul, Hⁿ(m(A)) = Hⁿ(λ⁻¹•A) = ‖λ⁻¹‖₊ⁿ • Hⁿ(A). As λ⁻¹ > 0, ‖λ⁻¹‖₊ = λ⁻¹ (Real.nnnorm_of_nonneg), and the NNReal scalar ‖λ⁻¹‖₊ⁿ acts on [0,∞] as multiplication by ofReal((λ⁻¹)ⁿ) = c (ENNReal.smul_def, ENNReal.ofReal_pow, Real.toNNReal_of_nonneg).
4. (Part (ii).) Both sides are measures, so it suffices to compare them on Borel sets B (Measure.ext). Right side: (c·D_#(Hⁿ⌞M))(B) = c·(Hⁿ⌞M)(D⁻¹B) (Measure.smul_apply, MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply) = c·Hⁿ(D⁻¹B ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_apply, D⁻¹B Borel). By step 3 this is Hⁿ(D(D⁻¹B ∩ M)), and D(D⁻¹B ∩ M) = B ∩ D(M) (Set.image_preimage_inter) = B ∩ η(M). Left side: (Hⁿ⌞η(M))(B) = Hⁿ(B ∩ η(M)) (Measure.restrict_apply). Hence (ii).
5. (Part (iii).) Put f(x) := ofReal θ(x) and g(y) := ofReal θ(a + λy). By (ii) the right side of (iii) is (c·D_#(Hⁿ⌞M)) with density g, which equals c·((D_#(Hⁿ⌞M)) with density g) (withDensity_smul_measure). So it suffices to show D_#((Hⁿ⌞M) with density f) = (D_#(Hⁿ⌞M)) with density g (then multiply by c). On a Borel set B: the left side is ((Hⁿ⌞M) with density f)(D⁻¹B) = ∫⁻_{D⁻¹B} f d(Hⁿ⌞M) (MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply, withDensity_apply); the right side is ∫⁻_B g d(D_#(Hⁿ⌞M)) (withDensity_apply) = ∫⁻ g d(D_#((Hⁿ⌞M)⌞D⁻¹B)) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map) = ∫⁻_{D⁻¹B} g(D(x)) d(Hⁿ⌞M)(x) (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map, which requires no measurability of g). By step 1, g(D(x)) = ofReal θ(a + λD(x)) = ofReal θ(x) = f(x), so the two integrals coincide. ∎
proof_key_steps: blowUpMap a λ = dilation a λ is the homeomorphism y ↦ −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y with a + λ·D(x) = x; so η(M) is Borel.
Hⁿ(D(A)) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·Hⁿ(A) from Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff scaling under smul and invariance under translation.
On Borel B: Hⁿ(B ∩ η(M)) = Hⁿ(D(D⁻¹B ∩ M)) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·Hⁿ(D⁻¹B ∩ M), which is (ii).
Pull the scalar out of withDensity and transport the density through the embedding (restrict_map, lintegral_map) using θ(a + λD(x)) = θ(x), which is (iii).

subproblem.title: Operator norm of an n-covector is at most P^n times its Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P, i.e. a continuous alternating n-linear map α : (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n). Let ‖α‖ be its operator norm (the norm of continuous alternating maps, ‖α‖ = sup{|α(v_0,…,v_{n−1})| : ‖v_k‖ ≤ 1}) and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i is the standard orthonormal basis. Then ‖α‖ ≤ P^n·|α|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), ‖α‖ ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ n * covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0, fact (F1), of the parent proof.
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i for i ∈ Fin P; for J : Fin n → Fin P write e∘J for the n-tuple (e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(n−1)}).
1. (Coefficient bound.) For every J : Fin n → Fin P we have |α(e∘J)| ≤ |α|.
 (a) If J is not injective, choose i ≠ j with J(i) = J(j). Then the tuple e∘J has equal entries in the positions i ≠ j, so α(e∘J) = 0 because α is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq), and 0 ≤ |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg).
 (b) If J is injective, let σ := Tuple.sort J; it is a permutation of Fin n with J∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). J∘σ is injective and monotone, hence strictly monotone (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective). Since α is alternating, α((e∘J)∘σ) = sign(σ)·α(e∘J) (AlternatingMap.map_perm for α.toAlternatingMap), and sign(σ) = ±1 (Int.units_eq_one_or), so |α(e∘J)| = |α(e∘I)| with I := J∘σ strictly increasing. Now α(e∘I)² is one of the summands in Σ_{I'} (if I' strictly increasing then α(e∘I')² else 0), all summands being ≥ 0, so α(e∘I)² ≤ that sum (Finset.single_le_sum) and therefore |α(e∘I)| ≤ √(sum) = |α| (Real.abs_le_sqrt).
2. (Multilinear expansion.) Let v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n and write v_k(i) for the i-th coordinate of v_k. Each v_k = Σ_{i ∈ Fin P} v_k(i)·e_i (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr for basisFun). By multilinearity (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_sum), α(v) = Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} α((v_k(J(k))·e_{J(k)})_k), and pulling out the scalars (ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_smul_univ for α.toContinuousMultilinearMap) α((v_k(J(k))·e_{J(k)})_k) = (Π_k v_k(J(k)))·α(e∘J).
3. (Estimate.) |v_k(i)| ≤ ‖v_k‖ for every coordinate (PiLp.norm_apply_le). By the triangle inequality (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs), |Π_k v_k(J(k))| = Π_k |v_k(J(k))| ≤ Π_k ‖v_k‖ and step 1, |α(v)| ≤ Σ_J (Π_k ‖v_k‖)·|α| = #(Fin n → Fin P)·|α|·Π_k ‖v_k‖ = P^n·|α|·Π_k ‖v_k‖ (Finset.sum_const, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin).
4. (Conclusion.) Since P^n·|α| ≥ 0 and |α(v)| ≤ (P^n·|α|)·Π_k ‖v_k‖ for all v, the operator-norm bound ContinuousAlternatingMap.opNorm_le_bound gives ‖α‖ ≤ P^n·|α|. The degenerate cases need no separate treatment: for n = 0 there is exactly one J (the empty map, strictly increasing) and the estimate reads |α()| ≤ |α|; for P = 0 < n there is no J, the sum is empty and α(v) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each basis coefficient α(e_{J(0)},…,e_{J(n−1)}) has absolute value ≤ |α|: it is 0 if J is not injective, and ± a strictly increasing coefficient otherwise (sort J, alternating sign).
Expand α(v) multilinearly in the standard basis: α(v) = Σ_J (Π_k v_k(J(k)))·α(e∘J).
Bound |v_k(i)| ≤ ‖v_k‖ and count the P^n terms: |α(v)| ≤ P^n|α|Π_k‖v_k‖.
Conclude ‖α‖ ≤ P^n|α| by ContinuousAlternatingMap.opNorm_le_bound.

subproblem.title: Currents L¹-close to a constant n-vector converge weakly, with a limsup mass bound
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm, ‖·‖ the operator norm on MultiVector P n = Λ_n(ℝ^P), ‖·‖ₑ its [0,∞]-valued version. Let X_k (k ∈ ℕ) and C be currents in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), ν_k, ν, μ_k measures on ℝ^P, τ_k : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P), ζ₀ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) and s ∈ ℝ such that: ν_k and ν are finite on compact sets; ∫ f dν_k → ∫ f dν for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ; limsup_k ν_k(K) ≤ ν(K) for every compact K; each τ_k is ν_k-a.e. strongly measurable; s ≥ 0 and |ζ₀(α)| ≤ s|α| for every n-covector α; for every R > 0, ∫⁻_{B̄_R(0)} ‖τ_k(x) − ζ₀‖ₑ dν_k(x) → 0; X_k(ω) = ∫ τ_k(x)(ω(x)) dν_k(x) and C(ω) = ∫ ζ₀(ω(x)) dν(x) for every test n-form ω; and M_W(X_k) = μ_k(W) for every k and every open W. Then X_k ⇀ C (WeaklyConvergesOn) and limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(K) for every compact K.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4, 6 (convergence Γ_k ⇀ C) and 10 (limsup bound) of the parent proof, in abstract form; there X_k = Γ_k, ν_k = Hⁿ⌞N_k, τ_k(y) = θ(a + λ_{φ(k)}y)ζ(a + λ_{φ(k)}y), ζ₀ = θ(a)ζ(a), s = θ(a) and μ_k are the mass measures of Γ_k. The upper bound M_G(Ξ_k) ≤ θ₀ν_k(G) used in step 10 there is proved directly here (step 4), so no constant-vector current Ξ_k is needed.
Notation: for a test form ω write ω̂ for its underlying form; δ_k(R) := ∫⁻_{B̄_R(0)} ‖τ_k − ζ₀‖ₑ dν_k, so δ_k(R) → 0 for every R > 0; f_ω(x) := ζ₀(ω̂(x)); g_{k,ω}(x) := (τ_k(x) − ζ₀)(ω̂(x)). Since ν_k and ν are finite on compact sets they are IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts (construct the instances from the hypotheses).
1. (Preliminaries for a test form ω.) ω̂ is continuous with compact support, so there are A ∈ ℝ with ‖ω̂(x)‖ ≤ A for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support) and R > 0 with tsupport ω̂ ⊆ B̄_R(0) (a compact set is bounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall; take R := max(R₀, 1)); ω̂(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport ω̂ (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). f_ω is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left, ζ₀(0) = 0), hence integrable for every measure finite on compact sets (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
2. (Error term.) Suppose ‖ω̂(x)‖ ≤ A for all x and tsupport ω̂ ⊆ B̄_R(0). Then ∫⁻ ‖g_{k,ω}‖ₑ dν_k ≤ ofReal(A)·δ_k(R): pointwise, for x ∈ B̄_R(0), ‖g_{k,ω}(x)‖ₑ ≤ ‖τ_k(x) − ζ₀‖ₑ·‖ω̂(x)‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(A)·‖τ_k(x) − ζ₀‖ₑ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opENorm), while g_{k,ω}(x) = 0 for x ∉ B̄_R(0); integrate (lintegral_indicator, lintegral_const_mul', lintegral_mono). Further g_{k,ω} is ν_k-a.e. strongly measurable: evaluation (L, v) ↦ L(v) is continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply), so Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ applies to τ_k − ζ₀ (a.e. strongly measurable) and ω̂ (continuous). Hence, if ofReal(A)·δ_k(R) < ∞, then g_{k,ω} is ν_k-integrable (finite lintegral of its norm); since τ_k(x)(ω̂(x)) = f_ω(x) + g_{k,ω}(x), X_k(ω) = ∫ f_ω dν_k + ∫ g_{k,ω} dν_k (integral_add), and |∫ g_{k,ω} dν_k| ≤ (ofReal(A)·δ_k(R)).toReal (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, ENNReal.toReal_mono).
3. (Weak convergence.) Fix ω and A, R as in step 1. ofReal(A)·δ_k(R) → 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul), so eventually ofReal(A)·δ_k(R) < 1 < ∞. For those k, step 2 gives X_k(ω) = ∫ f_ω dν_k + e_k with |e_k| ≤ (ofReal(A)·δ_k(R)).toReal, and (ofReal(A)·δ_k(R)).toReal → 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal at 0), so e_k → 0 (squeeze_zero_norm'). By hypothesis ∫ f_ω dν_k → ∫ f_ω dν = C(ω). Hence X_k(ω) → C(ω) (Tendsto.add, Tendsto.congr'). As ω was arbitrary, X_k ⇀ C.
4. (Mass bound.) Let k ∈ ℕ, R > 0 and G open with G ⊆ B̄_R(0). Then M_G(X_k) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν_k(G) + ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R). By definition M_G(X_k) is the supremum of ofReal(X_k(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n G, i.e. tsupport ω̂ ⊆ G and |ω̂(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; fix such ω (sSup_le). By the sibling covector_norm (cbr_ci_bl_covector_opNorm_le), ‖ω̂(x)‖ ≤ Pⁿ|ω̂(x)| ≤ Pⁿ for all x, and tsupport ω̂ ⊆ B̄_R(0). If ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R) = ∞ the bound is trivial. Otherwise step 2 with A = Pⁿ gives X_k(ω) = ∫ f_ω dν_k + ∫ g_{k,ω} dν_k and ∫ g_{k,ω} dν_k ≤ (ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R)).toReal. Moreover f_ω(x) ≤ |ζ₀(ω̂(x))| ≤ s|ω̂(x)| ≤ s for x ∈ G and f_ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ G, i.e. f_ω ≤ 1_G·s; as ν_k(G) ≤ ν_k(B̄_R(0)) < ∞, 1_G·s is integrable (integrableOn_const, IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator), so ∫ f_ω dν_k ≤ s·ν_k(G).toReal (integral_mono, integral_indicator_const). Therefore ofReal(X_k(ω)) ≤ ofReal(s·ν_k(G).toReal) + ofReal((ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R)).toReal) = ofReal(s)·ν_k(G) + ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le, ENNReal.ofReal_mul with s ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
5. (One thickening.) Let K be compact and r > 0. G_r := thickening r K is open with K ⊆ G_r ⊆ K_r := cthickening r K (self_subset_thickening, thickening_subset_cthickening), and K_r is compact (IsCompact.cthickening); choose R > 0 with K_r ⊆ B̄_R(0). By monotonicity of μ_k, the mass hypothesis and step 4, μ_k(K) ≤ μ_k(G_r) = M_{G_r}(X_k) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν_k(K_r) + v_k for all k, where v_k := ofReal(Pⁿ)·δ_k(R) → 0. Also limsup_k ofReal(s)·ν_k(K_r) = ofReal(s)·limsup_k ν_k(K_r) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) (ENNReal.limsup_const_mul_of_ne_top and the hypothesis on compact sets). Claim: limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(K_r). Let c > ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) and pick b with ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) < b < c (exists_between). Eventually ofReal(s)·ν_k(K_r) < b (eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt) and eventually v_k < c − b (v_k → 0 and c − b > 0, tendsto_order), so eventually μ_k(K) ≤ b + (c − b) = c; hence limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ c (limsup_le_of_le), and as c was arbitrary the claim follows (le_of_forall_gt_imp_ge_of_dense). (This route avoids ENNReal.limsup_add_le, which needs a countable-intersection filter.)
6. (Letting r ↓ 0.) K is closed and ν(K_1) < ∞ (K_1 compact), so ν(K_r) → ν(K) as r → 0 (tendsto_measure_cthickening_of_isClosed) and hence ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) → ofReal(s)·ν(K) along 𝓝[>] 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, ofReal(s) < ∞). Since limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(K_r) for every r > 0 by step 5, ge_of_tendsto gives limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(K). Together with step 3 this proves both conclusions. ∎
proof_key_steps: For a test form ω supported in B̄_R(0) with sup‖ω‖ ≤ A: ∫⁻|(τ_k − ζ₀)(ω)| dν_k ≤ A·∫⁻_{B̄_R(0)}‖τ_k − ζ₀‖ dν_k → 0, so X_k(ω) = ∫ζ₀(ω)dν_k + o(1).
∫ζ₀(ω)dν_k → ∫ζ₀(ω)dν = C(ω) by C_c-convergence, hence X_k ⇀ C.
With ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ Pⁿ|ω(x)| ≤ Pⁿ (covector_norm): M_G(X_k) ≤ s·ν_k(G) + Pⁿ∫⁻_{B̄_R(0)}‖τ_k − ζ₀‖dν_k for open G ⊆ B̄_R(0).
With G = thickening r K: limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ s·ν(cthickening r K) (ε-argument); let r ↓ 0 using ν(cthickening r K) → ν(K).

subproblem.title: Two-sided Hausdorff density bounds at a good point
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm, ‖·‖ the operator norm on MultiVector P n = Λ_n(ℝ^P) and ‖·‖ₑ its [0,∞]-valued version. Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel with θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M, ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) strongly measurable with |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and all n-covectors α, and for each x ∈ M an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(x)(β) = 1; let μ = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density x ↦ ofReal θ(x). Let a ∈ M and η₁ > 0 with (L) ofReal η₁ ≤ liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(a))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)), (U) limsup_{r↓0} Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) ≤ 1, and (D) (∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)} ‖θ(x)ζ(x) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ dHⁿ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) → 0 as r ↓ 0 (limits along 𝓝[>] 0). Then there is r₀ > 0 such that for all r with 0 < r < r₀: ofReal(η₁/(4θ(a)))·(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) and Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) ≤ 2·(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)).

Source: step 0 (fact (F2)) and step 1 of the parent proof.
Notation: ω_n := unitBallVolume n is the volume of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ; it is > 0 (Metric.measure_ball_pos) and < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). V(r) := ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ), so V(r) ∈ (0, ∞) for r > 0. θ₀ := θ(a) > 0 (a ∈ M); τ := θζ, i.e. τ(x) = θ(x)•ζ(x); τ₀ := τ(a) = θ(a)•ζ(a); o(r) := ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)} ‖τ − τ₀‖ₑ dHⁿ.
1. (F2, the half that is needed.) For x ∈ M: θ(x) ≤ θ₀ + Pⁿ‖τ(x) − τ₀‖. Take β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(x)(β) = 1. By the sibling covector_norm (cbr_ci_bl_covector_opNorm_le), ‖β‖ ≤ Pⁿ|β| ≤ Pⁿ, hence |(τ(x) − τ₀)(β)| ≤ ‖τ(x) − τ₀‖·‖β‖ ≤ Pⁿ‖τ(x) − τ₀‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm). Also ζ(a)(β) ≤ |ζ(a)(β)| ≤ |β| ≤ 1, so θ₀·ζ(a)(β) ≤ θ₀. Therefore θ(x) = θ(x)·ζ(x)(β) = θ₀·ζ(a)(β) + (τ(x) − τ₀)(β) ≤ θ₀ + Pⁿ‖τ(x) − τ₀‖. In [0,∞] (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal, ENNReal.ofReal_add, ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ofReal_norm_eq_enorm): ofReal θ(x) ≤ ofReal θ₀ + ofReal(Pⁿ)·‖τ(x) − τ₀‖ₑ.
2. (Mass of balls.) For every r: μ(B_r(a)) ≤ ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + ofReal(Pⁿ)·o(r). Indeed, by the formula for μ, withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict (balls are Borel), μ(B_r(a)) = ∫⁻_{M∩B_r(a)} ofReal θ dHⁿ. By step 1, which holds Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ B_r(a))-a.e. (ae_restrict_mem, lintegral_mono_ae), this is ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩B_r(a)} (ofReal θ₀ + ofReal(Pⁿ)·‖τ − τ₀‖ₑ) dHⁿ = ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + ofReal(Pⁿ)·∫⁻_{M∩B_r(a)} ‖τ − τ₀‖ₑ dHⁿ (lintegral_add_left for the constant, setLIntegral_const, lintegral_const_mul' as ofReal(Pⁿ) < ∞), and the last integral is ≤ o(r) because B_r(a) ⊆ B̄_r(a).
3. (Three eventual inequalities as r ↓ 0, i.e. in the filter 𝓝[>] 0.)
 (a) ofReal(η₁/2) < ofReal η₁ ≤ liminf μ(B_r(a))/V(r) by (L), so eventually ofReal(η₁/2) < μ(B_r(a))/V(r) (eventually_lt_of_lt_liminf).
 (b) o(r)/V(r) → 0 by (D) and ofReal(Pⁿ) < ∞, so ofReal(Pⁿ)·(o(r)/V(r)) → 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul); since ofReal(η₁/4) > 0, eventually ofReal(Pⁿ)·(o(r)/V(r)) < ofReal(η₁/4) (tendsto_order).
 (c) limsup Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/V(r) ≤ 1 < 2 by (U), so eventually Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/V(r) < 2 (eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt).
 The conjunction of (a), (b), (c) and r > 0 holds on a member of 𝓝[>] 0, so (Metric.mem_nhdsWithin_iff) there is r₀ > 0 such that (a), (b), (c) hold for every r with 0 < r < r₀.
4. (Conclusion for 0 < r < r₀.) As V(r) ∈ (0, ∞), (a), (b), (c) give ofReal(η₁/2)·V(r) ≤ μ(B_r(a)), ofReal(Pⁿ)·o(r) ≤ ofReal(η₁/4)·V(r) and Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) ≤ 2V(r) (ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt, ENNReal.div_lt_iff, mul_div_assoc). The last one is the asserted upper bound. For the lower bound write ofReal(η₁/2)V(r) = ofReal(η₁/4)V(r) + ofReal(η₁/4)V(r) (ENNReal.ofReal_add, add_mul). By step 2 and (b): ofReal(η₁/4)V(r) + ofReal(η₁/4)V(r) ≤ μ(B_r(a)) ≤ ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + ofReal(η₁/4)V(r); cancelling the finite summand ofReal(η₁/4)V(r) (ENNReal.add_le_add_iff_right) gives ofReal(η₁/4)V(r) ≤ ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)). Finally ofReal(η₁/(4θ₀)) = (ofReal θ₀)⁻¹·ofReal(η₁/4) (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos, ENNReal.ofReal_mul, field_simp), so ofReal(η₁/(4θ₀))·V(r) = (ofReal θ₀)⁻¹·(ofReal(η₁/4)V(r)) ≤ (ofReal θ₀)⁻¹·(ofReal θ₀·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a))) = Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) (ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel, ofReal θ₀ ∈ (0, ∞)). ∎
proof_key_steps: F2: for x ∈ M, θ(x) ≤ θ(a) + Pⁿ‖θ(x)ζ(x) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖, from the norming covector of ζ(x), |ζ(a)(β)| ≤ 1 and the covector_norm sibling.
μ(B_r(a)) ≤ θ(a)·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + Pⁿ·∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)}‖τ − τ₀‖ dHⁿ.
For 0 < r < r₀: μ(B_r(a)) ≥ (η₁/2)ω_nrⁿ (L), Pⁿ·o(r) ≤ (η₁/4)ω_nrⁿ (D), Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) ≤ 2ω_nrⁿ (U).
Cancel (η₁/4)ω_nrⁿ and divide by θ(a) to get Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) ≥ (η₁/(4θ(a)))ω_nrⁿ.

D_i is a measurable embedding — it is the homeomorphism y ↦ −λ_i⁻¹a + λ_i⁻¹y (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero followed by Homeomorph.addLeft) — and a + λ_i·D_i(x) = x. Consequently, for every Borel S, ν_i(S) = c_i·Hⁿ(M ∩ D_i⁻¹S) (Measure.smul_apply, MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply, Measure.restrict_apply, inter_comm); and for every g : ℝ^P → [0,∞] and Borel S, ∫⁻_S g dν_i = c_i·∫⁻_{M∩D_i⁻¹S} g(D_i(x)) dHⁿ(x) (Measure.restrict_smul, lintegral_smul_measure, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map, Measure.restrict_restrict).
2. (Balls and constants.) D_i(y) = λ_i⁻¹(y − a), so ‖D_i(y)‖ = λ_i⁻¹·dist(y, a) and, for R ∈ ℝ, D_i⁻¹(B̄_R(0)) = B̄_{λ_iR}(a) and D_i⁻¹(B_R(0)) = B_{λ_iR}(a) (inv_mul_le_iff₀, inv_mul_lt_iff₀). For R > 0, c_i·V(λ_iR) = V(R) because (λ_i⁻¹)ⁿ(λ_iR)ⁿ = Rⁿ (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, mul_pow); equivalently c_i = V(R)/V(λ_iR) (ENNReal.mul_div_cancel_right, V(λ_iR) ∈ (0, ∞)).
